summary.verdict: TWO results, one positive (architecture) and one HONEST caveat (study bias). POSITIVE: the SAME disease-agnostic substrate core that ranked pathogen proteins (SUBSTRATE1-4) now runs HUMAN-DISEASE target-ID across 3 cancers by swapping in Open Targets genetic/mutation/pathway evidence + a DepMap PAN-ESSENTIAL safety filter (the human analog of host-toxic — common-essential genes are toxic to inhibit), EXCLUDING pan-essential genes by construction (0 in every shortlist). **So 'any disease -> a query' spans INFECTIOUS (pathogens) AND NON-INFECTIOUS (cancer) through ONE governance layer — the architecture generalizes.** HONEST CAVEAT (the study-bias theme recurs): on RAW target recovery the genetic/mechanistic composite does NOT beat a study-popularity baseline (0/3; composite {'non-small ce': 38, 'breast carci': 9, 'melanoma': 18} vs popularity {'non-small ce': 67, 'breast carci': 28, 'melanoma': 30}) — because clinic-reached targets ARE the most-studied, so literature trivially recovers them (the SAME popularity confound that killed MET4's PPI signal). This does NOT contradict B34, whose finding was that genetic evidence beats popularity ONLY in a CONTROLLED (popularity-partialled, leave-disease-out) comparison — so a correct human-disease substrate needs a POPULARITY-CONTROL provider (residualize evidence against literature), exactly as the pathogen case needed the host-non-homology hard filter. The architecture is proven; the human-disease PROVIDERS must control study bias before their ranking is trustworthy. SCOPE: composition/governance on curated evidence (Open Targets B34; DepMap); human drug-response has hard ceilings (B10/B23); hypotheses with provenance, not validated targets; not clinical.
